title: Unauthenticated request gets 401 with a Bearer challenge
clause: A request without a token must be answered 401 and must carry a WWW-Authenticate header (RFC 6750 section 3). The MCP page requires 401 for invalid or missing tokens.
why: Without a 401 and a challenge, a client has no trigger to start authorization.
fix: Return HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... when no valid token is presented.

title: WWW-Authenticate parses cleanly: Bearer followed by auth-params
clause: The Bearer scheme must be followed by one or more auth-param values (RFC 6750 section 3); a challenge is auth-scheme then token68 or a comma list of auth-param (RFC 9110 grammar). An empty first element (a comma straight after the scheme) is not a valid auth-param.
why: Strict parsers stop at the empty first parameter and never see resource_metadata, so discovery fails for those clients (which clients is UNVERIFIED).
fix: Emit Bearer resource_metadata="...", scope="..." with no leading or doubled commas.

title: 401 challenge carries resource_metadata over https
clause: An MCP server must use the WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter or a well-known URI (MCP page). RFC 9728 requires TLS. The lab treats a non-https resource_metadata URL as a defect; loopback http is exempt so local mocks can be probed.
why: A plain-http metadata URL can be rewritten in transit, which lets an attacker choose the authorization server.
fix: Advertise an https URL for the protected resource metadata document.

title: 401 challenge hints the scope to request
clause: MCP servers SHOULD include a scope parameter in the WWW-Authenticate header so clients request least privilege.
why: Without it clients fall back to scopes_supported or guess, and over-request.
fix: Add scope="<space separated scopes>" to the 401 challenge.

title: Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) is served
clause: MCP servers MUST implement RFC 9728 protected resource metadata.
why: Clients find the authorization server only through this document.
fix: Serve JSON at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/path] and point resource_metadata at it.

title: Metadata names the resource and at least one authorization server
clause: resource is REQUIRED and must be identical to the resource URL the metadata was fetched for, otherwise the data MUST NOT be used (RFC 9728 section 3.3). MCP requires authorization_servers to hold at least one entry.
why: A mismatched resource lets a different server pose as this one; an empty list leaves clients with nowhere to go.
fix: Set resource to the exact MCP endpoint URL and list the authorization server issuer in authorization_servers.

title: Metadata is not served for paths that do not exist
clause: Lab heuristic (not a spec requirement): a metadata URL for a path that cannot be an MCP server should 404. If it answers 200, a probe cannot prove the target app exists, because a gateway may answer for any path.
why: A green metadata check from a wildcard gateway says nothing about the application behind it.
fix: Answer 404 for resource paths the gateway does not route, or accept that metadata checks only prove the gateway.

title: Authorization server metadata (RFC 8414 or OIDC discovery) is published and consistent
clause: Authorization servers MUST provide RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect discovery. The issuer value MUST be identical to the issuer used to build the metadata URL (RFC 8414 section 3.3).
why: Clients take the authorization and token endpoints from this document.
fix: Publish metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (or openid-configuration) with an issuer equal to the one in authorization_servers.

title: PKCE with S256 is advertised
clause: If code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, MCP clients MUST refuse to proceed; clients MUST use S256 when technically capable (RFC 7636 section 4.2). The ChatGPT guide says servers that omit S256 are unsupported.
why: A server that does not advertise S256 cannot be connected by compliant clients.
fix: Add code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"] to the authorization server metadata.

title: Issuer identification (RFC 9207): advertised, and returned in authorization responses
clause: An authorization server supporting RFC 9207 MUST put iss in every authorization response and MUST set authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported to true. MCP 2025-11-25 does not mention RFC 9207; the draft MCP page lists it as a standard. Treated as SHOULD here.
why: It defeats authorization server mix-up, and the ChatGPT guide ties its stable redirect URI to it.
fix: Set authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true and add iss=<issuer> to every authorization response, errors included.

title: Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) are supported
clause: Authorization servers and MCP clients SHOULD support CIMD, advertised as client_id_metadata_document_supported: true.
why: CIMD is the MCP default for clients with no prior relationship; without it clients fall back to DCR or ask the user.
fix: Support https client_id URLs and advertise client_id_metadata_document_supported: true.

title: Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) is offered
clause: Authorization servers MAY support DCR, kept for backwards compatibility. Not scored.
why: Some clients still register dynamically; this row shows which path your server offers.

title: Open dynamic registration validates redirect URIs and is gated or throttled
clause: Redirect URIs MUST be localhost or https (MCP page). RFC 7591 says an initial access token is required when the server limits who may register. Throttling is a lab heuristic, not a spec requirement (UNVERIFIED as a requirement). Mock targets only: the probe never registers a client.
why: Unlimited anonymous registration with arbitrary redirect URIs is a phishing and abuse surface.
fix: Require an initial access token, or reject non-https redirect URIs with invalid_redirect_uri and rate-limit registration.

title: The resource parameter (RFC 8707) is honoured
clause: MCP clients MUST send resource on authorization and token requests. The authorization server SHOULD audience-restrict the token to it and, for an unacceptable resource, should answer invalid_target (RFC 8707 section 2).
why: If the server ignores resource, tokens are not bound to this MCP server and can be replayed elsewhere.
fix: Copy the requested resource into the token audience and reject unknown resources with invalid_target.

title: A token issued for another audience is refused with 401
clause: MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the audience; invalid tokens MUST get HTTP 401.
why: Accepting any valid token turns the server into a token-passthrough confused deputy.
fix: Check aud against the server's canonical resource URI and answer 401 on mismatch.

title: Too little scope gets 403 insufficient_scope with the needed scope
clause: On insufficient scope the server SHOULD answer 403 with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="..." and resource_metadata.
why: That challenge is what lets a client step up instead of failing.
fix: Return 403 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<needed>", resource_metadata="...".

title: Metadata is current: advertised endpoints exist and caching is short
clause: Lab heuristic (UNVERIFIED as a requirement): the endpoints the metadata advertises must not answer 404/410, and metadata should not be cacheable for more than a day.
why: Stale metadata sends clients to endpoints that moved, and long caches keep them there.
fix: Update the metadata when endpoints move and keep Cache-Control max-age at or below 86400.
